Proceed-
ings
Mr. Lea appeared for the police
Mr. Tseu Ky! Vung appeared for the P.S. Bureau.
Mr. Loh Tsing-Foong appeared for the accused.

Mr. Tseu:-The P.S. Bureau has wired Hankow to send down all the
evidence and necessary documents relating to this case, but they
have not yet arrived.

Mr. Loh:-The accused has now been detained a long time and the
Hankow authorities should have the documents here by this time.

Judge:-The representative of the P.S. Bureau at the last hearing
stated that the documents would arrive from Hankow within two weeks,
the Court has also sent them a despatch to send the documents to
this Court, but they have not yet arrived.

Mr. Tseu:-This is the fault of the Hankow Authorities, not the P.S.
Bureau. I did not know about the case when it came up at the last
hearing, that is the reason I did not attend the Court.

Mr. Loh:-As Mr Tseu and the P.S. Bureau cannot produce any evidence
that the accused is a communist, I ask the Court to release the ac-
cused.

Judge, to Mr. Tseu:-Before the arrest of the accused, did the P.S.
Bureau receive a circular warrant from the Hankow Authorities.
The Court have received no reply from them as yet, to the despatch
they sent them. If the Court remands the case again, could you
tell us how many days it would be, before the documents arrive from
Hankow.

Mr. Tseu:-I cannot answer that, I ask the Court to set a date for a
further trial.

Mr. Loh:-This Court has jurisdiction over this case, as there has
been no evidence brought against the accused, I ask the Court to
release him.

Mr. Lea:-The police have not charged the accused, if the documents
have not arrived from Hankow, and the P.S. Bureau cannot produce any
evidence against the accused from two weeks today, I will ask the

Court to release the accused.

Accused:-I have now been detained a long time, there has been no evidence has been produced against me,and as I am not a communist and am now sick,I ask the Court to release me.

Mr.Tseu:-I know the P.S.Bureau cannot produce the evidence today, but that does not mean that the accused is not a communist.

I do not mind if the accused is released on reliable security.

Procurator:-I suggest that the accused be released on security.

Judge:-If the Court releases the accused,can you guarantee his appearance at the next hearing,Mr.Loh.

Mr.LOH:-The school principle is in Court and he will guarantee his appearance.

Tseu Kyl Hoo:-I am the principle of the Dau Tsung School,564 Avenue Rd.where the accused is employed. I will guarantee the accused because I know he is not a communist.

Tai Tsong Yau:-I am a teacher in a school for politics,and have known the accused for three years,and I know he is not a communist. I am a member of the Kuomintang,if the accused was a communist, I would have had him arrested long ago.

Judge:-Will you also guarantee the appearance of the accused at the next hearing.

Mr.Tai:-I will guarantee the accused as the P.S.Bureau has produced no evidence and the accused has been detained a long time,therefore I think he should be released at once.

Mr.Tseu Kyl Yau:-If the Court thinks that we are fit to guarantee the accused,then we will do so.

Judge:-Then You are both responsible for the appearance of the accused at the next hearing.

Mr.Tseu Kyl Yau:-We will be responsible for the accused up to one month from today.

Judge Zau,to guarantors:-Remember you both liable to imprisonment if you allow the accused to abscond.

Extract from Daily Intelligence Report of December 8, 1931.

Acting on the authority of a warrant issued at the
instance of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, the Municipal
Police at 12.15 a.m. December 8 arrested one Zung Yuen Zung
(陈润生) at No.175 Sinza Road, on a charge of propagating
communism. A search of his room resulted in the seizure of
three books of a pro-communist nature. The accused will
appear before Court on the morning of December 8, when an
application for his extradition to the Chinese Authorities
will be made.

Moore and Tcheremshansky and party attached to the Special Branch came to the Station on the authority of a Shanghai Special District Court Arrest and Search Warrants No. 6105 & 6110 to search and seize certain communistic literature at 175 Sinza Road and if any found to arrest Tung Tai Oong (陈补安). This warrant may be executed at night in accordance with article 148, Sect. 2 of Criminal Procedure.

At 12.15 a.m. 8-12-32, the above mentioned party with the assistance of D.S. Nuncarrow and C.D.C. 229 raided the above premises and broke through the wooden partition in time to see the accused attempting to escape by way of the verandah but was arrested by Tsang Ching Tai (张静泰) of the S.P.S.B. as he was dropping to the ground. A search of the accused's room revealed 5 communistic books which will be produced in Court.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zung Yuen Sung (陈芸生)
native of Kiangsi taken by me D.S. Moore
at Sinza St'n on the 8-12-28 and interpreted by Clark Chao.

My name is Zung Yuen Sung, native of Nanchong, Kiangsi, and
my age is 26 years. When I was 7 years of age I commenced
studying in the Primary School in my native place. I remained
there until I was 14 years of age, and then went to Nanchong
College, Hupeh, until I was 18 years of age. Then I commenced
studying German in the same college until I was 20 years of age.
From that time until I was 24 I was teaching the Chinese Language
in my native place.

Following this I came to Shanghai and resided in Rue Amiral
Bayle, 24 Zung Ching Fang, French Concession and was a student
for 1 year in the Chuen Chi University, Robison Road, and then
was engaged for 1 year as a teacher in the Poong Yah Middle
School, Yates Road. About this time I removed to Tai Hwa Li
Alleyway, N/Honan Road and was unemployed except for sending
articles to various Shanghai Newspapers and magazines. I then
taught geography for the next 6 months in the Chung Tuh Girls
School, Avenue Road and then arithmetic in the Tao Chang Girls'
School, first in Chowai and later at 564 Avenue Road, where I
am at present engaged.

I have been residing at the Ting Zung Tai Tin Smiths' Shop,
175 Sinza Road, where I was arrested, for the past two months
along with my wife and 2 years of age child. My wife left me
three days ago taking the child with her.

I have never taken part in any Communistic demonstrations or
movements and have never belonged to any Communist Party in which
I have no interest.

The books found in my room by the Police were bought by a
